analysis:
The only change is documentation in docs/reference/configuration.md. At head lines 413-414, the DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_DEADLINE_MODE row now says the default is `enforce`, that only exactly `off` disables it, and that `[backend] prefill_deadline_mode` in provider.toml takes precedence. The patch also adds a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES row: on by default, disabled by 0/false/off/no, and forwarded to the launchd provider job. No code, key handling, attestation, encryption or authorization paths change in this diff.

Threat relevance: the change records that prefill-deadline admission is enforced by default, which matches availability concerns such as T-010 and T-029. It does not weaken any control. It touches no prefix-cache behavior (T-041) and no App Attest, coordinator-provider or key boundary (TB-002, TB-011, A-003, A-016).

Unverified contract: I could not check the claimed Swift behavior (PrefillDeadlineMode.resolve, DeadlineAdmissionFixes) because those sources are not supplied. If the code differs, the documentation would be wrong, but that would be drift and not a security regression. The doc line 410 note says a lower video pruning rate yields more tokens than the coordinator estimates. This is unchanged context, not new in this PR.

A reviewer of the implementation PR should confirm that default-enforce and the launchd forwarding of DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES match the code. No threat-model updates are required by this docs-only change.
